issues.description: Command name inconsistent with existing quickmark-/bookmark- verb-noun convention
issues.detail: Existing commands are quickmark-save, quickmark-add, bookmark-load (singular noun first, verb second). New commands are quickmarks-reload, bookmarks-reload (plural noun, different shape). This complects naming-by-verb with naming-by-collection in the same namespace. Pick one form; the simple thing is bookmark-reload / quickmark-reload to match what's already there.

issues.description: reload() silently keeps stale state if the file read fails midway
issues.detail: reload() clears self.marks first, then re-reads via _init_lineparser. If parsing raises, the manager is left with an empty marks dict and a changed signal that hasn't fired yet, while disk still has the old data. The value (parsed marks) and the identity (self.marks) are being mutated in place rather than swapped atomically. Build the new dict first, then assign and emit.

issues.description: Parsing logic duplicated between __init__ path and reload(); should be one function
issues.detail: Before this change, __init__ inlined the parse loop. Now reload() contains it and __init__ delegates. Good direction, but the loop body (skip blanks/comments, _parse_line) is the actual unit of work and deserves its own pure-ish helper that takes lines and returns a dict. Then reload becomes: read, parse-to-value, swap, emit. Values and effects separated.

issues.description: Feature scenarios are unnamed and don't assert the actual reload behavior
issues.detail: Both new Scenario: lines have no title and only check that the info message printed. That tests the message, not the reload. The interesting test is: change the file on disk, run the command, observe the new mark is present and the old is gone. Test what the command is *about*, not that a string was emitted.

issues.description: changed signal now fires on every reload even if nothing changed
issues.detail: reload() always emits self.changed, even when the file contents are identical to current marks. Subscribers will re-render or re-save unnecessarily. The value semantics here are clear: emit only when the new marks value differs from the old one. Cheap dict comparison, avoids spurious work downstream.

review.summary: The feature itself is small and reasonable — exposing an existing capability (re-read from disk) as a command. The decomposition is partially right: pulling the parse loop out of __init__ into reload() is the move. But it stops halfway. The parse loop still mutates self.marks in place rather than building a new value and swapping, so a mid-parse failure leaves the manager in a half-cleared state — classic place-oriented programming biting under error conditions. Naming is COMPLECTED with two conventions (verb-noun and plural-noun-verb) in the same command namespace; pick one. Tests verify the message string, not the actual reload behavior, which is TDD-AS-DESIGN testing the wrong surface. Decision: COMPLECTED — close to simple, needs one more pass to separate the parsed value from the identity-swap.
